title: EEGProbe: Do Vision-Language Models Really Understand EEG? A Benchmark for Signal-Grounded EEG Signals Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2611.20779v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown strong multimodal capabilities across scientific and biomedical domains, yet their ability to understand electroencephalography (EEG) signals remains unclear. We introduce EEGProbe, a signal-grounded benchmark for evaluating whether general-purpose VLMs can extract and reason from minimally processed, channel-wise EEG without task-specific feature engineering or EEG-specific adaptation. EEGProbe contains 620 EEG-centered questions across 13 subtasks and three capability categories: EEG Signal Classification, EEG Cross-modal Alignment, and EEG Neurophysiological Reasoning. To reduce shortcut-based answering, EEGProbe preserves the temporal structure of the recordings where possible, minimizes benchmark-induced processing, and applies signal-necessity testing followed by expert verification. translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型在科学和生物医学领域已展现出强大的多模态能力，但它们理解脑电信号的能力仍不明确。我们提出了EEGProbe，这是一个基于信号的基准，用于评估通用视觉语言模型能否从经过最少处理的、逐通道的脑电信号中提取信息并进行推理，而无需任务特定的特征工程或脑电专用适配。EEGProbe包含620个以脑电为核心的问题，涵盖13个子任务和三大能力类别：脑电信号分类、脑电跨模态对齐和脑电神经生理推理。为减少基于捷径的回答，EEGProbe在可能的情况下保留记录的时间结构，最小化基准引入的信号处理，并采用信号必要性测试与专家验证相结合的方式。我们在统一的零样本协议下评估了11个具有代表性的开源与闭源视觉语言模型。表现最强的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出EEGProbe——一个包含620个问题、13个子任务和三大能力类别的基于原始脑电信号的基准，用于在无任务特定处理的条件下系统评估视觉语言模型是否真正具备理解脑电信号的能力。
en_tdlr: We introduce EEGProbe, a signal-grounded benchmark with 620 questions across 13 subtasks and three capability categories, to systematically evaluate whether vision-language models can truly understand minimally processed EEG signals without task-specific adaptation.
